title: Log event renamed compliance.review_unparseable -> compliance.review_unparsable, breaking the stable observable contract
detail: Project conventions state structured event names are a stable observable contract (BigQuery/Sentry). Renaming silently orphans any dashboard/alert keyed on the old name, and the spelling change is unrelated to issue #172.
recommended_fix: Keep the legacy event name, or rename with a documented migration: update all dashboards/queries/references in the same commit and scope the change out of the #172 fix.

title: Verdict-stamp mechanism never exercised end-to-end — every test seeds the slot instead of running the callbacks that write it
detail: The fake run_node writes nothing, so _stamp_review_verdict and the callback_context.state-to-session merge are never invoked. If callback state writes never reach the session dict, every test passes while the production cross-check silently never fires.
recommended_fix: Add a test driving the real judge callback (log_boundary_compliance_review) with a fake callback_context and assert the stamp lands in session.state before the guard reads it.

title: Clean-stamp cross-check cannot fire under the diff's own failure model, and the stamp is read through the same view that hid the review
evidence:
+            verdict = read_review_verdict(state, "boundary")
+            if verdict is not None and verdict.get("passed") is True:
detail: Fix premise: output_key writes land in ctx.session.state, so review=None at finalize means the judge produced nothing — and a no-output judge writes no stamp. The clean-stamp branch fires only under an unstated asymmetric failure, and it reads through the same state view that 'failed'.
recommended_fix: Either demonstrate the asymmetric failure (callback delta surviving when output_key does not) with a regression test, or drop the cross-check and rely on the direct session.state reads.

title: Verdict stamp is never cleared, unlike STATE_COMPLIANCE_JUDGE_META; stamp fields violation_count/parseable are write-only
detail: The new stamp lingers in session.state for the whole invocation, quarantined only by judge_kind filtering, temp: scoping and per-run overwrite — fragile if a future gate reads it without a fresh stamp. violation_count/parseable have no consumer.
recommended_fix: Pop STATE_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_VERDICT in both gates' finally blocks alongside STATE_COMPLIANCE_JUDGE_META, and drop the unread fields or surface them in the guards' log extras.

title: read_review_verdict docstring promises None for malformed shapes; implementation returns any dict with a matching judge_kind
evidence:
+    Returns the stamp dict when it records a verdict for ``judge_kind``
+    (``"boundary"`` / ``"final"``), else ``None`` (missing, wrong judge, or a
+    malformed shape).
+    verdict = state.get(STATE_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_VERDICT)
+    if not isinstance(verdict, dict):
+        return None
+    if verdict.get("judge_kind") != judge_kind:
+        return None
+    return verdict
detail: A stamp missing 'passed' (or with a non-bool passed) passes the read and is returned as valid; callers currently fail closed, but the doc/impl mismatch invites a trusting future caller. Also no return type annotation.
recommended_fix: Validate the stamp shape in read_review_verdict (require a bool 'passed' key) so the docstring matches the implementation, and add a return type annotation.

title: Boundary gate's judge->scrub->re-judge loop shows no state-write migration, unlike the final gate's STATE_FINAL_OUTPUT write-back
detail: The final gate's write-back was migrated to ctx.session.state; the boundary gate's scrub section (hidden between hunks) shows no analogous migration. If it writes state via ctx.state, the stale-snapshot bug persists on the boundary re-judge path.
recommended_fix: Verify the boundary gate's scrub/write-back writes to ctx.session.state like the final gate; migrate it if it still writes via ctx.state.
